title: Split augmented coherent simplicial diagrams are absolute colimits
statement:
Use the quasicategories, nerves, coherent diagrams, mapping spaces and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in universes large enough for the categories below. Write $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ for $n\geq0$ and $[-1]=\varnothing$. Let $\Delta$ be the ordinary category of the nonempty $[n]$ and monotone maps, and let $\Delta_+$ also include $[-1]$. Let $\Delta_{-\infty}$ have objects $[n]$ for $n\geq-1$ and morphisms the monotone maps $\{-\infty\}\cup[m]\to\{-\infty\}\cup[n]$ fixing the new least element $-\infty$. Embed $\Delta_+$ into this category by extending a monotone map to fix $-\infty$, so that no ordinary element maps to $-\infty$. An augmented coherent simplicial diagram $X:N(\Delta_+)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal E$ is called split if it extends to $N(\Delta_{-\infty})^{\mathrm{op}}$. Every such split diagram is a colimit diagram with vertex $X_{-1}$. Explicitly, for every $e\in\mathcal E$, the augmentation induces a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(X_{-1},e)\simeq\lim_{[n]\in\Delta}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(X_n,e).$$
For every coherent functor $Q:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F$, the augmented diagram $QX$ is also a colimit diagram. No existence of other colimits in either category is assumed.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Notation 4.7.2.1, Definition 4.7.2.2, Remarks 4.7.2.3-4, printed pp. 677-678; the colimit theorem is HTT Lemma 6.1.3.16 as explicitly stated there. Online source read; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.
